title: Policy-aware model intake and escrowed pin lane playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are asking for deterministic model versioning, regulatory audit trails, and a clear path for bringing new open models into production without exposing their traffic to unvetted variants. Current model intake treats all requests similarly, which increases time-to-serve for regulated requests and creates uncertainty around pinning/deprecation decisions.

Objective: Design a playbook and priority lane that routes policy-sensitive model intake (regulatory, HIPAA/PCI-adjacent, legal obligations) through an escrowed pin lane and a hardened eval gate. The lane should produce an auditable intake record, a prescribed evaluation checklist (safety, quality, privacy), and pre-approved rollback/fallback policies. The goal is predictable SLAs for regulated onboarding while retaining throughput for standard catalog additions.
background: We already have general model intake flows and a set of eval gates for catalog additions. Enterprise customers often request pinned variants or extended stability guarantees. Ad-hoc pin requests are creating manual overhead for engineering and compliance. There is no explicit escrow/retention path for model binaries or a defined SLA for enterprise pin approval. Existing tickets in the backlog reference fast-paths and sponsor-driven approvals but not a policy-centric lane.
proposed_solution:
1) Create a new intake label 'policy-sensitive' that can be set by Solutions/CS/PM when a request has regulatory or contractual implications.
2) Add an 'Escrowed Pin Lane' in the catalog intake UI and triage workflow that:
   - Requires a documented rationale, regulatory references, and intended retention window.
   - Locks the model to an escrow state pending security and legal sign-off.
   - Stores a checksum and metadata snapshot of the model artifact in customer-scoped escrow storage (metadata only if the model is public).
3) Harden eval gate for this lane: mandatory checks for privacy leakage (PSI), known steerability tests, token-level cost regression, and targeted regression tests against customer prompt sets.
4) Define SLA & calendar: initial triage within 5 business days, security/legal review within 10 business days, engineering readiness checklist and rollout within 20 business days (accelerations possible for sponsored enterprise customers).
5) Implement functional rollback/fallback policy: auto-fallback routes to approved compatible model family when safety or perf regressions detected post-rollout.
6) Instrumenting audit trail: every action (pin, unpin, sign-off) writes an immutable audit event captured in Console logs and included in customer-facing onboarding packet.
acceptance_criteria: Policy-sensitive label exists in intake UI and can be attached at submission time
Escrowed Pin Lane documented in intake playbook and visible in triage dashboard
Eval gate checklist implemented with automated tests for privacy/psi and performance regressions
SLA milestones (5/10/20 days) tracked and surfaced in intake dashboard
Audit trail events emitted for pin/unpin/sign-offs and included in onboarding artifacts
Fallback routing implemented for at least two model families and smoke-tested in staging
success_metrics: Median time-to-approval for policy-sensitive requests drops to <= 20 business days
Number of manual follow-ups (CS/Eng) per policy-sensitive intake reduces by 50%
Post-rollout safety incidents for pinned models remain < 1% over first 90 days
Customer satisfaction (CSAT) with regulated onboarding > 4.2/5 for pilot customers
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): Run lane manually for 3 enterprise customers, iterate on checklist (4 weeks)
Phase 1: UI + dashboard changes + automated eval gate integration (8 weeks)
Phase 2: Escrow storage integration and audit retention policy + legal SOPs (12 weeks)
Phase 3: Wider launch with SLA enforcement and opt-in for sponsored customers (16 weeks)
stakeholders: Engineering: Marco Li (assignee), Runtime Infra, Catalog Services
Customer Pilot Group: 3 regulated customers (names redacted)
open_questions: Should escrow store full model binaries for public open models, or only checksums and provenance metadata?
What retention period do customers require by default for escrowed artifacts (90/180/365 days)?
Can we extend current eval infra to run customer-provided prompt suites in a privacy-preserving way?
How will pricing/contracting reflect escrowed pin SLA and storage costs?
